chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, who said:

There came out from Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, when al-Zubayrī was killed: “This is the recompense of one who forged a lie against Allah concerning His Awliya'. He claimed that he would kill me and that I would have no posterity. So how did he see the power of Allah?” And a son was born to him, whom he named M Ḥ M D, in the year two hundred and fifty-six.

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad, the kunyah of the Imam عليه السلام referred to in the report
key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهِ: His Awliya', meaning Allah’s chosen guardians
key_terms.الزُّبَيْرِيُّ: al-Zubayrī, the individual whose death is mentioned in the narration
key_terms.جَزَاءُ: recompense or requital for one’s deed
key_terms.عَقِبٌ: posterity, offspring, or surviving line of descent

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the response of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام to the claim that he would have no successor?
ai.summary: This report records a statement issued from Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام after the death of al-Zubayrī, declaring his fate to be the recompense for fabricating false claims against Allah regarding His Awliya'. The text also affirms the birth of the Imam’s son, presenting it as a manifestation of the divine power that disproved the opponent’s claim that the Imam would leave no progeny.
